assumptions.rationale: English is the de facto business language in the US; no specific source was cited for this profile field, so it is recorded as an assumption, not evidence.
assumptions.value: English is the primary business language.

assumptions.rationale: The size-distribution evidence implies procurement varies by firm size, but the specific procurement norms by size band are not sourced to a study.
assumptions.value: Procurement varies sharply by company size. Formal vendor processes and security/procurement reviews are common at enterprise scale; small firms decide faster, often with the owner or founder.

assumptions.rationale: No single published typical B2B software budget exists; budgets vary by orders of magnitude between a nonemployer firm and an enterprise.
assumptions.value: No single typical B2B software budget. Budgets vary by orders of magnitude between a nonemployer firm and an enterprise; let the scenario price drive the sensitivity.

source.name: U.S. Small Business Administration, Office of Advocacy, Frequently Asked Questions About Small Business (2026)

evidence.value: 36.2 million small businesses = 99.9% of all US businesses (Census 2022 data). Small businesses employ 62.3 million people = 45.9% of private-sector workers. About 6.4 million employer firms plus about 29.8 million nonemployer firms.

source.name: U.S. Small Business Administration, Office of Advocacy

evidence.value: SBA generally defines a small business as an independent business with fewer than 500 employees, but size standards vary by industry (NAICS) and can include revenue thresholds.

source.name: U.S. Small Business Administration / U.S. Census Bureau, via USAFacts and ScienceStream

evidence.value: Firms with fewer than 20 employees make up nearly 90% of all employer businesses. Large enterprises (500 or more employees) are less than 1% of all businesses.
